title: Crispy Garlic Chicken
seoTitle: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas Lite | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Charred peppers and onions with spiced chicken strips—no heavy oil
subtitle: Charred peppers and onions with spiced chicken strips—no heavy oil
description: Chicken breast strips roast with tri-color bell peppers and red onion on two sheet pans. Warm tortillas and lime finish the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Garlic Chicken in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and mix spice blend
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Combine chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, and salt in a small bowl until evenly blended. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season chicken and vegetables
steps.instruction: Toss chicken strips with half the spice blend, lime juice, and 2 tbsp oil. Toss peppers and onion with remaining spice and 1 tbsp oil until coated.

steps.title: Spread on sheet pans
steps.instruction: Divide chicken and vegetables across two parchment-lined half-sheets in a single layer. Strips should not overlap or they will steam instead of roast. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Roast until chicken is cooked
steps.instruction: Roast 18–22 minutes, stirring once halfway, until chicken reads 165°F and pepper edges blister and char lightly. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest and serve with warm tortillas
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes off heat. Vegetables should still have bite; chicken should be juicy when sliced, not chalky in the center. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Cut chicken uniform so thin ends do not dry before thick pieces finish.
A cast-iron under the sheet pan boosts bottom char if your oven runs cool.
Offer Greek yogurt instead of sour cream for a lighter topping that still cools spice.
tonightSpread: Warm flour or corn tortillas in foil.
Pico de gallo, shredded lettuce, and light shredded cheese at the line.
leftovers: Fajita filling in breakfast burritos with scrambled eggs.
Toss leftovers over romaine for a taco salad with crushed baked tortilla chips.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Build-your-own format keeps everyone happy. Less grease than traditional fajitas but still delivers char and smoke from a hot oven.
mealPrepNotes: Slice peppers and onion into uniform strips for even roasting. Marinate chicken up to 4 hours in the walk-in. Station: Broil the last 2 minutes if you want more char without overcooking lean breast strips. Station: Keep tortillas wrapped in foil in a low oven so they stay pliable at the line. Station: Portion chicken and veg into hotel pans for fast assembly during a short dinner window.
